text: The Nasdaq fell 1.4% and the S&P 500 0.3% as Alphabet closed 12.6% lower after its results, ending the S&P's three-day winning streak.
After the close, Intel fell roughly 18–23% and Amazon about 7% on their outlooks, and Nasdaq-100 futures dropped about 2%.
Gold fell about 1% to near $4,025 and silver about 3.1% to $52.18 after 3.4% GDP growth and firm inflation kept a December Fed hike in play.
Gold miners fell harder than gold: GDX lost about 3.1% to $81.33 and GDXJ about 3.3%.
The 10-year yield fell more than 8 bp to about 4.96%, back below 5%, as the tech selloff sent money into bonds.
The Bank of Japan held rates at 1.25% in an 8–1 vote, with one member wanting a hike; the yen firmed about 0.4% to near 157.1 per dollar.
Brent slipped 44 cents to settle at $114.88 a barrel on renewed US-Iran peace efforts.
The VIX closed up about 1.7% at 17.2 after dipping to 16.2 during the day.
